title: Stability anchor and surge suppression scratchpad
content:
Quick summary:
- Purpose: lightweight personal playbook for rolling changes while keeping a small always-stable anchor cohort and suppressing request surges that destabilize autoscaling. Not a formal doc — notes + checklist for upcoming rollout.
- Primary risks we want to control: noisy neighbor spikes, warmup-induced latency cliffs, KV-cache churn causing memory pressure, token-cost regressions.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Can route by client-id / api-key; can attach metadata to requests for cohorting.
- We have two compatible model variants: model-v2-quant (faster) and model-v2-ref (baseline stable).
- Autoscaler reacts to queue depth and GPU util; cold starts add ~600ms p50 if below steady-state.

Concepts / patterns proposed:
1) Stability anchor cohort (SAC)
   - Always hold 1-2% of production traffic pinned to model-v2-ref (baseline). Acts as sentinel for regressions.
   - Anchor traffic should be distributed across clients (not just internal tools) to reflect real patterns.
   - Instrument per-anchor metrics and compare to current rollout cohort in near-real time (1m buckets).

2) Surge suppression window (SSW)
   - When routing a new cohort, temporarily apply request smoothing to that cohort: per-client rate cap + small token budget per minute to avoid spikes.
   - If a client bursts above threshold, ephemeral queuing/backpressure with a short retry-after header instead of unbounded retries.

3) Warmup grace + progressive concurrency
   - Start new instances with a low concurrency cap for 5–10 minutes and increase linearly to target.
   - Pre-warm top N cached KV prefixes from production logs for high-volume clients where feasible.

Preflight checklist (must be green before flip):
- [ ] Canary unit tests and smoke tests pass in staging (Jenkins job: infra/canary-smoke #112).
- [ ] Perf profile of model-v2-quant under realistic payloads (seq len dist) shows p95 < 2200ms.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboard created: SAC vs cohort side-by-side with p50/p95, error rate, token cost, queue depth.
- [ ] Rollback playbook validated with a dry-run (no traffic change) to ensure canary-bump and pin flip commands work.
- [ ] Ops channel and pager rotation notified; runbook pinned in the channel.

Rollout steps (gradual):
1) Create cohort config: 0.5% traffic to cohort-A (new model) + 1% SAC pinned to v2-ref.
2) Enable surge suppression for cohort-A (cap: 5 concurrent requests per client, 60k tokens/min client cap).
3) Monitor 1m buckets for 15 minutes: p50/p95, errors, GPU queue depth, container OOMs.
4) If stable, double cohort size every 30–60m until 10%; at 10% switch to 5% increments.
5) At each step, run a light synthetic test sweep (cold-start + hot-path) to surface regression patterns.
6) If any metric crosses thresholds (see thresholds below) → immediate step-down to previous stable cohort size and run deep triage.

Metric thresholds (triggering events):
- Error rate: >0.5% absolute increase compared to SAC sustained for 3 consecutive 1m buckets.
- Latency: p95 increase > 35% vs SAC for 5m rolling window.
- Cost: token cost per 1k tokens increases > 15% and coincides with latency or errors.
- Queue depth / warm starts: queue depth > 2x baseline and new instance starts > 50% of requests for >10m.
- Memory: container memory usage increases > 20% and OOM observed even once.

Fast rollback / mitigation steps:
- Immediate actions (can be done by on-call):
  * Move cohort-A traffic back to SAC (pin traffic to v2-ref) — command: rwd ctl rollout scale --cohort cohort-A --percent 0
  * Apply temporary global surge suppression: per-client concurrency 2 and token cap 30k/m.
  * Blacklist offending client-ids (short term) if a single client causes the spike.
- Post-incident: collect full traces, KV cache metrics, and top-N inputs that triggered regressions.

Telemetry & dashboards (must have):
- Live compare: SAC vs rolling cohort p50/p95, errors, tokens-per-request, cost-per-request.
- Per-region instance churn (starts/min), queue depth, and autoscaler decision logs.
- Top failing client ids and top failing endpoints.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How to represent composite regressions (small latency bump + slight cost increase) as a single decision score? (idea: weighted score with latency weight = 0.6, error weight = 0.3, cost weight = 0.1)
- Are per-client token caps feasible for enterprise customers (SLA implications)?
- Should SAC be static (same clients always) or rolling sampling of clients to avoid bias?

Quick notes from recent experiments:
- Observed pattern: warm-up RMSE in KV-hit rate correlates strongly with p95 spikes during rollout. Pre-populating top prefixes reduced p95 by ~20% in testbed.
- Autoscaler hysteresis tweak (increase stabilizationWindow to 60s) reduced thrash when we increased cohort size quickly.

Next actions (me / this week):
- [ ] Wire SAC metric panel and alert rule (Maya to review).
- [ ] Prototype per-client surge suppression in the router (Lucas volunteer to PR).
- [ ] Generate a short runbook snippet for on-call with exact rollback commands and where to check KV-cache heatmaps.
- [ ] Do a mock drill with a 0.5% cohort next Tue (dry-run traffic routing only).

Notes-to-self: keep anchor cohorts small but representative; err on the side of suppression rather than immediate scaling when testing new variants; document exact rollforward maths in a separate calc sheet when we have final numbers.

Triage checklist template (post-mortem starter):
- Start time / end time / cohort id.
- Which metric tripped? p95 / error / cost / OOM.
- Top 5 client-ids by traffic during incident.
- Hot inputs sample + model debug logs.
- Corrective action taken + how long to restore baseline.

End of scratchpad.
